summary: Initial discovery for PLG/self-serve Redwood API. EchoWave is evaluating hosted quickstart and wants to understand time-to-first-token, free credits, and whether they will likely need Dedicated or Private in 6-12 months for data residency. Security (SOC2, SSO, KMS) and latency/cost tradeoffs are top priorities.
topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs
Security: SOC2, SSO, KMS, audit logs
Performance benchmarks and latency vs cost
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Thanks everyone for joining, I'm Maya from Redwood, this is Diego from our SE team. quick intro?
[00:12] Samir Patel: Yeah hi all, Samir here, CTO at EchoWave. we're exploring embedding search + customer support summarization, hope to keep latency under 200ms for short queries, and cost's a factor.
[00:29] Claire Huang: Hey, Claire, ML eng. main pain is time-to-first-token, we want devs to try Redwood with minimal setup, free credits would help.
[00:45] Diego Ramos: cool, quick note — our PLG quickstart is designed for that: API keys, free credits, sample prompts, SDKs. most teams can get first token in minutes.
[01:02] Derek Lee: how does onboarding work for hosted vs dedicated? we have HIPAA-ish constraints and may need VPC later.
[01:18] Maya Chen: Hosted gets you fastest time-to-value; Dedicated reserved capacity is for predictable throughput and data isolation; Private is our VPC/on-prem option for strict residency. you can start hosted and then move to Dedicated.
[01:35] Samir Patel: ok, if we start hosted, what's guaranteed around data retention and encryption?
[01:42] Diego Ramos: We encrypt at rest and in transit, can integrate customer KMS for Dedicated/Private. For hosted, we have SOC2 controls and audit logs; if you need dedicated key control we recommend Dedicated or Private.
[01:58] Claire Huang: curious about token-level cost breakdown — can we see per-route/model token counts?
[02:06] Maya Chen: yes Redwood Console exposes token-level cost and latency; you can filter by route, model, token type.
[02:15] Priya Rao: also curious about function calling and streaming, we want tool-calling for customer workflows.
[02:21] Diego Ramos: both supported in hosted API, streaming responses and function/tool calling works.
[02:30] Samir Patel: performance — what's realistic latency for short prompts on hosted?
[02:37] Diego Ramos: depends on model and sequence length; typical 0.5-1x baseline for small open models, but our runtime does batching and KV cache. for 200 token responses we often hit ~150-350ms p95 on hosted for optimized models; Dedicated can tighten that with pinned capacity.
[02:58] Samir Patel: that sounds promising. are there benchmarks or a quick spreadsheet?
[03:03] Maya Chen: yes I'll send our benchmark sheet and a quickstart checklist + free credits link.
[03:10] Claire Huang: what about model selection and quantization recommendations?
[03:14] Diego Ramos: Redwood Optimize provides model and quantization recs by workload; for PLG you can start with curated open models in our catalog.
[03:25] Derek Lee: integration path — do we need infra changes or just API calls?
[03:29] Diego Ramos: mostly API calls for hosted. for Dedicated/Private you'll coordinate with our ops for network setup (VPC peering, firewall rules), and we provide deployment templates.
[03:45] Samir Patel: any gotchas when moving from hosted to Dedicated?
[03:49] Maya Chen: plan for data migration and KMS integration, model pinning changes, and capacity sizing. we help with migration runbooks.
[03:58] Priya Rao: security checklist — SSO/SAML, RBAC?
[04:03] Diego Ramos: yes SSO/SAML and RBAC available; audit logs and retention policies configurable.
[04:12] Samir Patel: ok next steps? we'd like a trial so our devs can hit it, and a tech deep dive for Diego's team to run perf tests.
[04:20] Maya Chen: we'll provision free credits and a trial org, Diego will schedule the benchmark demo. I'll send security docs and the pricing sheet after this call.
[04:31] Claire Huang: perfect, I'll prepare sample queries and a small dataset for perf testing.
[04:38] Diego Ramos: One small note — when you share sample prompts please include expected QPS and p95 latency targets so we can recommend model/quantization and batching config.
[04:50] Samir Patel: noted. thanks everyone.
[04:54] Maya Chen: thanks, we'll follow up with the links and calendar invite.
[05:00] (call ends)

Notes: transcript auto-generated; minor mis-transcriptions possible (eg. KV cache sometimes transcribed as KV cash). There was brief crosstalk around 03:25-03:40.
notes: Customer leans PLG/self-serve to validate before committing to Dedicated. Primary success criteria: sub-300ms p95 on short prompts, clear cost per token, secure key management. Pilot likely in next 2-4 weeks.
